title: Dead-on-Arrival Handling for Hardware Procurement Units
content:
**Time limit.** A Hardware Procurement unit that fails out of the box is handled as dead on arrival only when it is reported within the order type's dead-on-arrival window in calendar days after delivery. The period is counted in calendar days from the delivery date, that date being day 0, and the window includes its last day. The delivery date that starts the count is the one on the system record of the order the unit came on.

**Authorization.** A dead-on-arrival return is authorized for the failed units on the authorized contact's signed return request, even on non-returnable orders, and no restocking fee applies where the order type waives restocking on confirmed dead-on-arrival units.

**Inspection outcome.**

| Inspection result | Remedy |
|---|---|
| Failure confirmed, order type remedy "replace or credit" | The units are replaced, or credited at their unit price where the client chooses credit |
| Failure confirmed, order type remedy "replace only" | The units are replaced |
| Failure not confirmed | The units are shipped back with no credit |

**After the window.** A failure reported after the dead-on-arrival window goes to the manufacturer warranty, and Stratton Bay neither replaces nor credits it.

**Boundary cases (abstract).** With a 15-day window, a failure reported on day 15 after the delivery date is within the window; one reported on day 16 goes to the manufacturer warranty. With a 30-day window, day 30 is within and day 31 is not.
